boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Babson College
boards.description: Build an under-21-safe late-night ritual board. Every card needs a currently verifiable destination, a direct source supporting late availability, and a conservative explanation of why it matters near this campus. Do not invent student habits, signature orders, popularity, or current hours. Bars and 21+-only venues are prohibited.

cards.title: The Campus Living Room
cards.subtitle: 21 Babson College Dr
cards.notes: Visit the Global Lounge for late-night study sessions or grab food at the various dining stations located on the first floor.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, offering dining, study spaces, and social areas open late for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Reynolds is described as the central hub for late-night cravings and mobile ordering, housing multiple dining options.
cards.access_notes: Dining hours vary by station; the building remains accessible to students via OneCard for study and lounge use.

cards.title: Korean Street Food at Reynolds
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Order Korean-inspired bowls and wings through the mobile app for a quick late-night meal on campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular campus dining spot in Reynolds serving Korean-American street food, including signature chicken and rice platters.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick-N-Bap is listed as a dining option in Reynolds Campus Center for late-night cravings.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Reynolds Campus Center; check the mobile ordering app for current nightly closing times.

cards.title: Late Night Study at Horn
cards.subtitle: Babson College Drive
cards.notes: Utilize the quiet study nooks and collaborative spaces in the newly renovated library commons during late hours.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic resource center on campus, providing extensive study spaces and technology access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Horn Library is a hub of campus activity with study spaces and a Resource Center accessible to students.
cards.access_notes: Student OneCard required for entry; hours typically extend late during the academic semester.

cards.title: Pub Fare at Trim Hall
cards.subtitle: Trim Dining Hall
cards.notes: Enjoy pub-style food and a social atmosphere with pool tables and theme nights in this on-campus venue.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dining and social space located in Trim Dining Hall, offering a casual environment for students to unwind.
cards.evidence_claim: Roger's Pub & Grille is an on-campus option for food and social gatherings, located in Trim Dining Hall.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students for food; alcohol service is restricted to those 21+ with valid ID.

cards.title: Essentials at Olin Hall
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall
cards.notes: Pick up snacks, beverages, and personal care items at this convenient on-campus market located in Olin Hall.
cards.short_summary: A campus essentials store providing quick access to food and toiletries for students, especially those in the graduate programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Market at Olin is a campus essentials store with snacks and beverages located in Olin Hall.
cards.access_notes: Check the Boost Mobile App for current market hours and mobile checkout options.

cards.title: Late Night Ice Cream
cards.subtitle: 63 Central St
cards.notes: Walk to Wellesley Square for a late-night scoop of ice cream or a frozen yogurt until 11 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: A local favorite for ice cream and coffee, located in the heart of Wellesley Square and open late for dessert runs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wellesley Square location of J.P. Licks is open daily from 10 AM to 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM every night of the week.

cards.title: Midnight Pizza Delivery
cards.subtitle: 868 Worcester St
cards.notes: Order delivery or carryout for a late-night study break; this location serves the Babson and Wellesley community until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A reliable late-night food option offering pizza, wings, and sides with delivery directly to campus residence halls.
cards.evidence_claim: The Domino's at 868 Worcester St in Wellesley is open until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: 868 Worcester Street in Wellesley - Domino's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM for delivery and carryout.

cards.title: Local Pizzeria Run
cards.subtitle: 7 Washington St
cards.notes: Visit this neighborhood staple for a slice of pizza or a hot sub before they close for the evening.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing local pizzeria known for its fresh ingredients and community involvement, located near the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley North End Pizza is a neighborhood favorite providing delivery and takeout to the local area.
cards.source_title: About Us - Wellesley North End Pizza
cards.access_notes: Check current daily hours for evening closing times; typically open for dinner and late-evening orders.

cards.title: Late Night Essentials
cards.subtitle: 188 Linden St
cards.notes: Grab late-night snacks or health essentials at this pharmacy location open until 10 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: A convenient stop for students to pick up groceries, snacks, and over-the-counter needs in Linden Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The CVS at 188 Linden St is open daily from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
cards.source_title: CVS Pharmacy at 188 Linden St. Wellesley, MA 02482
cards.access_notes: Store is open until 10:00 PM; pharmacy hours may differ.

cards.title: Inter-Campus Late Shuttle
cards.subtitle: Hollister Parking Lot
cards.notes: Catch the shuttle between Babson, Olin, and Wellesley campuses, with service running until midnight on Saturdays.
cards.short_summary: A shared transportation service connecting the three local colleges, allowing students to access facilities and events across campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: The BOW shuttle operates until 12:07 AM on Saturdays, connecting Babson, Olin, and Wellesley.
cards.access_notes: Free for students with valid college ID; check the live tracker for real-time arrival info.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, collaborative labs, and quiet retreats that define daily life for Babson students beyond the standard admissions highlights.

cards.title: Global Lounge
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Visit this 'campus living room' to study on comfortable furniture or borrow outdoor lawn games and board games between classes.
cards.short_summary: A central social and study hub in the Reynolds Campus Center featuring flexible seating and game rentals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Global Lounge in Reynolds Campus Center is described as a 'campus living room' where students can hang out, study, and borrow lawn or board games.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during Reynolds Campus Center operating hours; accessible via student OneCard.

cards.title: Weissman Foundry
cards.subtitle: Collaborative Maker Space
cards.notes: Access the woodshop, digital fabrication studio, or social kitchen to prototype products and collaborate with Olin and Wellesley students.
cards.short_summary: A cross-campus maker space for Babson, Olin, and Wellesley students to create and prototype ideas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weissman Foundry is a collaborative space featuring a woodshop, digital fabrication studio, and social kitchen for student prototyping.
cards.access_notes: Open to students from Babson, Olin, and Wellesley; specific workshop hours apply for equipment use.

cards.title: Horn Library Quiet Nooks

cards.access_notes: Quiet zones are strictly enforced; check library website for current semester hours.

cards.title: Graduate Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Relax or watch TV in this ground-floor lounge, which serves as the primary social hub for the graduate student community.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for graduate students located on the ground floor of Olin Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Lounge on the ground floor of Olin Hall is a place for graduate students to relax and watch TV.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for graduate student use; accessible during Olin Hall building hours.

cards.title: Glavin Family Chapel
cards.subtitle: Nondenominational Sanctuary
cards.notes: Step into this glass-walled sanctuary for a moment of quiet meditation or to attend diverse spiritual services.

cards.title: Babson Ceramics Studio
cards.subtitle: Sorenson Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Join as a member to access pottery wheels and kilns; the studio is located within the Sorenson Visual Arts Center in Trim Hall.
cards.short_summary: A fully equipped ceramics studio available to the Babson community for a semester fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The Babson Ceramics Studio is located in the Sorenson Visual Arts Center within Trim Hall and offers memberships to students.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 8 a.m.–10 p.m. daily via OneCard for registered members.

cards.title: Park Manor Central Basement
cards.subtitle: Creative & Study Rooms
cards.notes: Utilize the music practice room, dance studio, and quiet study areas tucked away in the basement of this residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use basement space in Park Manor Central featuring music and dance facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Manor Central's basement includes study rooms, a music room, and a dance studio for student use.
cards.access_notes: Building access restricted to residents; facilities may be bookable for other students.

cards.title: The Horizon Room
cards.subtitle: Trim Dining Hall Extension
cards.notes: Head to this 200-seat extension of the main dining hall for a slightly quieter meal or group meeting during peak hours.
cards.short_summary: A large seating extension of the Trim Dining Hall used for meals and student gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Horizon Room is an extension of the Trim dining area providing an additional 200 seats for students.
cards.source_title: Babson College Trim Dining Hall | Gilbane Building Company
cards.access_notes: Open during Trim Dining Hall meal service hours.

cards.title: Kerry Murphy Healey Park
cards.subtitle: Centennial Park
cards.notes: Relax in the Adirondack chairs surrounding the iconic Babson World Globe in this park established for the college's centennial.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped park featuring the historic Babson World Globe and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Kerry Murphy Healey Park is home to the Babson World Globe and offers a space for students to sit and enjoy the outdoors.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor park; globe rotation is scheduled periodically.

cards.title: International Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot to read or study in this dedicated room located within the bustling campus center.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading and study room located inside the Reynolds Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reynolds Campus Center contains an international reading room as a dedicated space for students.
cards.source_title: Babson College | Reynolds Campus Center | William Rawn Associates Architects
cards.access_notes: Open during Reynolds Campus Center hours; intended for quiet study.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Babson College's campus with these social activities and spaces that require no admission or purchase, from global landmarks to high-tech maker labs.

cards.title: Visit the Giant Spinning Globe
cards.subtitle: Kerry Murphy Healey Park
cards.notes: Snap a photo with this 25-ton rotating landmark. It is free to visit and serves as a central campus meeting point in the heart of the park.
cards.short_summary: A historic 28-foot diameter rotating globe located in a public campus park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Babson World Globe is a signature photo spot on campus located in Kerry Murphy Healey Park and is free to visit.
cards.source_title: Kerry Murphy Healey Park - Babson Centennial
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to the public as an outdoor landmark.

cards.title: Browse Contemporary Art Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Hollister Hall
cards.notes: Walk through rotating exhibitions featuring professional and student artists. The gallery is open to the public on weekdays with no admission fee.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery hosting professional exhibitions and artist talks.
cards.evidence_claim: Hollister Gallery exhibits are free and open to the public, typically open Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Join a Prototyping Workshop
cards.subtitle: 9 Map Hill Drive
cards.notes: Attend free training sessions for 3D printing, laser cutting, or woodshop tools. This collaborative space is open to all Babson, Olin, and Wellesley students.

cards.evidence_claim: The Weissman Foundry offers free training sessions on equipment like laser cutters and vinyl cutters for students.
cards.access_notes: Open to Babson, Olin, and Wellesley students; check website for semester hours.

cards.title: Play Billiards or Air Hockey
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Campus Center
cards.notes: Challenge friends to a game of pool or air hockey. The game room is a central social hub for students to unwind between classes.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge area equipped with pool tables, air hockey, and arcade games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reynolds Campus Center features a Game Room with pool tables, air hockey, and arcade games for student use.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with a Babson OneCard during building hours.

cards.title: Find Quiet in the Multi-Faith Chapel
cards.subtitle: Forest Street
cards.notes: Visit this architectural landmark for personal reflection or meditation. The space features two walls of glass overlooking a peaceful wooded area.
cards.short_summary: A non-denominational sanctuary used for spiritual services and quiet meditation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Glavin Family Chapel offers a nondenominational sanctuary for gatherings and personal reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community for services and quiet reflection.

cards.title: Study in the Light-Filled Commons
cards.subtitle: Horn Library
cards.notes: Grab a seat in the 10,000-square-foot glass-walled addition. It is a popular spot for group collaboration and quiet individual study.
cards.short_summary: A modern, bright study and social hub located within the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Babson Commons at Horn Library provides 10,000 square feet of study space and is a hub of campus activity.
cards.source_title: Babson Horn Library Renovations | Finegold Alexander Architects

cards.title: Walk the Indoor Track
cards.subtitle: Webster Center
cards.notes: Stay active regardless of the weather on the 200-meter indoor track. It is located on the second floor and is free for students to use.
cards.short_summary: A six-lane indoor running and walking track available for recreational use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Webster Center features a six-lane, 200-meter indoor track restricted to runners and walkers with no charge for students.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with a Babson OneCard during facility hours.

cards.title: Hang Out on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Park Manor Quad
cards.notes: Relax on the grass or join spontaneous lawn games. This central green space is the site for major free campus events like Founder's Day.
cards.short_summary: The primary outdoor social lawn for undergraduate students on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Manor Quad is a popular spot for students to hang out and hosts events like Founder's Day with free food and lawn games.
cards.source_title: 26 Tips for the Class of 2026 - Babson College
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Ride the Free Shuttle to Boston
cards.subtitle: Campus Pickup Points
cards.notes: Catch a free ride to the city on weekends. The shuttle connects the Wellesley campus to downtown Boston for easy off-campus exploration.
cards.short_summary: A complimentary bus service for students traveling between campus and Boston.
cards.evidence_claim: A free shuttle runs from the campus to Boston on the weekends, requiring a Babson OneCard to board.
cards.access_notes: Available Thursday-Sunday; check the current schedule on the Babson website.

cards.title: Relax in the Graduate Lounge
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Unwind on comfortable furniture or watch TV with classmates. This lounge serves as the primary social 'living room' for graduate students.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated social space for graduate students to connect and relax.
cards.evidence_claim: Olin Hall offers a Graduate Student Lounge on the ground floor where students can relax and chat with friends.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for graduate students; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: Silent Zone on the Third Floor

cards.evidence_claim: The center features an amphitheater, classroom, and collaboration spaces for students in the FME course.
cards.access_notes: Located in a residence hall; primarily for first-year student use.

cards.subtitle: Learning center in Horn Library

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the primary commercial corridors and micro-districts surrounding Babson College, from the boutiques of Wellesley Square to the retail hubs of Needham Street.

cards.title: Central Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Square District
cards.notes: Visit the heart of Wellesley for local favorites like JP Licks and Wellesley Books, located just two miles from the Babson campus.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Square is the town's primary downtown area, featuring a mix of independent boutiques and established national retailers.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Square is home to 60+ stores, restaurants, and services, including JP Licks and Wellesley Books on Central Street.
cards.source_title: The one and only Wellesley Square
cards.access_notes: Public street with metered parking and proximity to the Wellesley Square MBTA Commuter Rail station.

cards.title: Linden Street
cards.subtitle: Linden Square Shopping District
cards.notes: Stop by this modern retail hub for a meal at Tatte Bakery & Cafe or to pick up groceries at the flagship Roche Bros. market.
cards.short_summary: Linden Square is a pedestrian-friendly shopping destination anchored by Roche Bros. and featuring numerous dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Linden Square features boutique stores like Tatte Bakery + Café and is anchored by Roche Brothers.
cards.source_title: Linden Square: Wellesley's Premier Shopping & Dining Destination
cards.access_notes: Open-air shopping center with ample free parking lots for customers.

cards.title: Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Hills Commercial Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the historic Hills district, home to the Wellesley Hills Branch Library and local cafes near the MBTA station.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Hills is a commercial village located near Babson Park, offering local services and transit access.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Hills is a commercial village that includes the Wellesley Hills Branch Library and is bordered by Babson Park.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Wellesley Hills MBTA Commuter Rail station and Route 16.

cards.title: Church Street
cards.subtitle: Church Square District
cards.notes: Dine at Popovers at Church Square or browse the local boutiques in this historic corner of Wellesley Square.
cards.short_summary: Church Square is a distinct shopping and dining area within the broader Wellesley Square district known for its historical vibe.
cards.evidence_claim: Church Square is a destination for shopping and dining with a historical vibe, featuring Popovers at Church Square.
cards.access_notes: Features free parking for visitors and is walkable from Central Street.

cards.title: Needham Street
cards.subtitle: Newton Highlands Retail Corridor
cards.notes: Head to this major retail strip for big-box essentials at Marshalls, TJ Maxx, and the Newton Nexus shopping center.
cards.short_summary: Needham Street in Newton is a major commercial corridor providing extensive retail and dining options for the region.
cards.evidence_claim: Newton Nexus is located on Needham Street, which connects Route 128 to Route 9 and features retailers like Marshalls.
cards.access_notes: Heavy commercial traffic; most shopping centers offer large free parking lots.

cards.title: Great Plain Avenue
cards.subtitle: Needham Town Center
cards.notes: Explore the shops of Needham Center, including The Run House and various local eateries along this main thoroughfare.
cards.short_summary: Great Plain Avenue serves as the primary commercial spine of Needham, offering a village-style shopping experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Great Plain Avenue in Needham is home to businesses like Proud Mary and The Run House.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Needham Center MBTA Commuter Rail station.

cards.title: Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Lower Falls District
cards.notes: Visit the border of Wellesley and Newton for specialty shops and the scenic Charles River crossing.
cards.short_summary: Wellesley Lower Falls is a historic commercial area located at the intersection of Washington Street and the Charles River.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Lower Falls is a commercial village featuring office buildings and retail assets along Washington Street.
cards.source_title: Major Wellesley commercial properties change hands in Lower Falls & Rte. 9
cards.access_notes: Located near the intersection of Route 16 and Route 128.

cards.title: Highland Avenue
cards.subtitle: Needham Crossing District
cards.notes: Check out this growing innovation district, home to major tech headquarters and the nearby TripAdvisor office.
cards.short_summary: Needham Crossing is a modern mixed-use district on Highland Avenue featuring corporate offices and retail services.
cards.evidence_claim: Needham Crossing is a modern, connected, mixed-use urban layout on Highland Avenue home to TripAdvisor and other companies.
cards.access_notes: Easily accessible from Route 128 via the Highland Avenue interchange.

cards.title: Worcester Street
cards.subtitle: Route 9 Commercial Strip
cards.notes: Access quick dining options like Cheesy Street Grill along this busy commuter route connecting Wellesley to Natick.
cards.short_summary: Worcester Street (Route 9) is a major regional thoroughfare lined with commercial plazas and dining establishments.
cards.evidence_claim: Wellesley Crossing at 100 Worcester Street features Craft Food Halls and other dining services.
cards.access_notes: High-speed traffic area; primarily accessible by car with dedicated parking lots.

cards.title: Grove Street
cards.subtitle: Wellesley Square South
cards.notes: Find local services and dining like Amarin of Thailand on this street connecting Wellesley Square to residential areas.
cards.short_summary: Grove Street is a key commercial street in Wellesley featuring a variety of local businesses and professional offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Grove Street is home to businesses like Anderson's Jewelers and Amarin of Thailand.
cards.access_notes: Walkable from the main Central Street shopping area.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Explore the unique customs and rituals that define the entrepreneurial spirit and history of Babson College.

cards.title: Founder's Day
cards.subtitle: Celebrating Roger Babson since 1947
cards.notes: Join the community for apple-themed treats and carnival games to honor Roger Babson's legacy and his admiration for Sir Isaac Newton.
cards.short_summary: An annual fall celebration honoring the college's founder with apple-themed events and community gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Founder's Day is a fall tradition since 1947 that honors Roger Babson with activities including apple-themed lunch and Founder's Fest.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in September across the Wellesley campus.

cards.title: The Spinning World Globe
cards.subtitle: A 25-ton symbol of global reach
cards.notes: Visit the restored 28-foot rotating globe in Kerry Murphy Healey Park, a landmark commissioned by Roger Babson in 1947.
cards.short_summary: A massive, rotating globe that serves as a central campus landmark and symbol of Babson's global perspective.
cards.evidence_claim: The Babson Globe, weighing 25 tons and 28 feet in diameter, was restored and moved to Kerry Murphy Healey Park in 2019.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors in Kerry Murphy Healey Park, accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Great Beaver Hunt
cards.subtitle: Finding 100 hidden beavers
cards.notes: Search the campus for 100 hidden toy beavers during Spirit Week to win prizes and show your Babson pride.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide scavenger hunt for hidden beaver figurines held during the annual Spirit Week.
cards.evidence_claim: The Great Beaver Hunt involves hiding 100 beavers around campus for students to find and win prizes during Spirit Week.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Student Life Events - Babson College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during Spirit Week leading up to Back to Babson.

cards.title: Late-Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Fueling finals with faculty service
cards.notes: Head to Trim Dining Hall before finals to enjoy breakfast served by your favorite faculty and staff members.
cards.short_summary: A finals-week tradition where faculty and staff serve breakfast foods to students late at night in the dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Late-Night Breakfast is held at the end of the fall semester at Trim Dining Hall, with food served by faculty and staff.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Student Life Events - Babson College
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during finals week at Trim Dining Hall.

cards.title: Cruickshank Race for Shelter
cards.subtitle: Running for a cause since 2003
cards.notes: Participate in this annual 5K run during Family and Friends Weekend to support service immersion trips and Habitat for Humanity.
cards.short_summary: A charitable 5K race held annually to raise funds for student service trips and local housing initiatives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cruickshank Race for Shelter is an annual 5K held during Family and Friends Weekend, named after alumnus Bill Cruickshank.
cards.source_title: Babson on the Run · Babson Thought & Action
cards.access_notes: Typically starts at Hollister Hall during Family and Friends Weekend in October.

cards.title: Buffoonery
cards.subtitle: Graduate student variety show
cards.notes: Watch graduate students perform skits and songs that playfully poke fun at the Babson experience and faculty.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring variety show coordinated by graduate students featuring good-natured irreverence and skits.
cards.evidence_claim: Buffoonery is an annual spring variety show coordinated by Babson graduate students featuring skits and songs.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring, primarily for the graduate student community.

cards.title: The Great Babson Bake-Off
cards.subtitle: Sweet relief during finals
cards.notes: Sample treats baked by faculty and staff and vote for your favorite during this Grad Rejuvenation Week event.
cards.short_summary: A baking competition where faculty and staff provide treats for graduate students during final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: The bake-off began in 2011 as part of Grad Rejuvenation Week, where staff and faculty bake treats for students to vote on.
cards.access_notes: Held during Grad Rejuvenation Week in the fall and spring semesters.

cards.title: Together Under the Tent
cards.subtitle: The heart of homecoming
cards.notes: Gather with alumni and families under the big tent for the signature celebration of Reunion and Homecoming weekend.
cards.short_summary: The central social gathering of the Back to Babson weekend, bringing together the entire college community.
cards.evidence_claim: Back to Babson brings the community 'Together Under the Tent' for Reunion, Homecoming, and Family Weekend.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in September, typically on the Park Manor Quad.

cards.title: MLK Jr. Legacy Day
cards.subtitle: Honoring diversity and inclusion
cards.notes: Attend guest lectures and award ceremonies that celebrate the values of Dr. King and recognize community leadership.
cards.short_summary: An annual day of reflection and celebration focused on diversity, inclusion, and the teachings of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
cards.evidence_claim: Martin Luther King Jr. Legacy Day includes guest speakers, leadership awards, and a creativity contest.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Student Life Events - Babson College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in January to coincide with MLK Day.

cards.title: Last Bingo
cards.subtitle: A final senior week tradition
cards.notes: Join your graduating class in Knight Auditorium for one final high-stakes game of bingo before commencement.
cards.short_summary: A popular Senior Week event where graduating undergraduates gather for a final communal bingo game.
cards.evidence_claim: Last Bingo is a signature event for undergraduates during Senior Week, held in Knight Auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduating undergraduate seniors during Senior Week in May.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Babson College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack at Park Manor
cards.subtitle: Step 1: Move-In Day Arrival
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned time to move into the Park Manor residence halls, the central hub for first-year living near the library and dining hall.
cards.short_summary: The primary residential area for first-year students at Babson College.
cards.evidence_claim: New student move-in typically occurs on the Thursday of orientation week, with students assigned specific times by Residence Life.
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to residential students with a valid Babson OneCard.

cards.title: The Community Dinner
cards.subtitle: Step 2: Thursday Evening Welcome
cards.notes: Join fellow new students and families for an outdoor dinner on the Upper Fields to officially celebrate your arrival in the community.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor gathering space used for large-scale orientation welcome events.
cards.evidence_claim: A Community Dinner is held on the Upper Athletic Fields from 5-7 p.m. on the first day of orientation to welcome students and families.
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and their families during orientation week.

cards.title: Meet Roger the Dog
cards.subtitle: Step 3: Thursday Night Social
cards.notes: Head to the Park Manor Quad for ice cream and games to celebrate the birthday of Roger, Babson's community resource dog.
cards.short_summary: A traditional orientation social event featuring the campus resource dog.
cards.evidence_claim: Roger's Birthday Bash is a scheduled orientation event at 8 p.m. featuring Ben & Jerry's ice cream and the community resource dog.
cards.access_notes: Held outdoors in the quad; rain location is typically Knight Auditorium.

cards.title: Breakfast at Trim
cards.subtitle: Step 4: Friday Morning Fuel
cards.notes: Start your first full day of programming with breakfast at the main campus dining hall, known for using local produce in its dishes.
cards.short_summary: The primary all-you-care-to-eat dining facility on the Babson campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Trim Dining Hall is the primary dining option for meals throughout the day on campus for the Babson community.
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal plan or individual payment for entry.

cards.title: The Campus Living Room
cards.subtitle: Step 5: Friday Midday Break
cards.notes: Visit the Global Lounge to relax between orientation sessions, check your mail, or grab a coffee at the on-site Dunkin'.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, housing the bookstore, mailroom, and student org offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Donald W. Reynolds Campus Center is described as the campus living room and houses the Campus Store and mail services.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; specific office hours for mail and the bookstore vary.

cards.title: Find Your Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Step 6: Friday Afternoon Exploration
cards.notes: Explore the recently renovated library commons to find your preferred study spot before classes begin on Monday.
cards.short_summary: The main academic research facility featuring a 10,000-square-foot Commons addition.
cards.evidence_claim: Horn Library features a Resource Center and a 10,000-square-foot Commons addition for student research and innovation.
cards.source_title: Babson Horn Library Renovations | Finegold Alexander Architects
cards.access_notes: Babson OneCard required for entry after certain hours; check LibCal for current daily hours.

cards.title: Win Some Swag
cards.subtitle: Step 7: Friday Night Tradition
cards.notes: Participate in this high-energy student tradition hosted by the Campus Activities Board to win prizes and meet your new classmates.
cards.short_summary: A popular recurring social event for students often held during welcome weeks.
cards.evidence_claim: Pajama Bingo is a notable campus event hosted by the Campus Activities Board (CAB) that students frequently attend.
cards.source_title: A Day in the Life of a Babson College Senior #BabsonUnscripted
cards.access_notes: Typically held in Trim Dining Hall or Knight Auditorium; check the CAB Instagram for locations.

cards.title: Saturday Morning Workout
cards.subtitle: Step 8: Saturday Fitness
cards.notes: Visit the Lunder Fitness Center or the indoor track to stay active. Students have free access to the gym and pool with their ID.
cards.short_summary: The main athletics and recreation complex on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Webster Center includes the Lunder Fitness Center, Morse Pool, and an indoor track for student use.
cards.access_notes: Valid Babson OneCard required for entry to the fitness center and pool.

cards.title: Prototype Your Ideas
cards.subtitle: Step 9: Saturday Afternoon Creativity
cards.notes: Check out the collaborative maker space where you can use 3D printers, a woodshop, and a social kitchen for cross-campus projects.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative studio for Babson, Olin, and Wellesley students to create and prototype.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weissman Foundry is a space for students to create and collaborate, featuring a woodshop and digital fabrication studio.
cards.access_notes: Open to students from the BOW (Babson, Olin, Wellesley) partnership.

cards.title: Reflect and Recharge
cards.subtitle: Step 10: Sunday Morning Quiet
cards.notes: Visit this multi-faith space on the hillside for a moment of peace or to attend a service before the first week of classes begins.
cards.short_summary: An inclusive place of worship and home to the Office of Religious and Spiritual Life.
cards.evidence_claim: The Glavin Family Chapel hosts events and services for people of all faiths, cultures, and traditions.
cards.source_title: Graduate Religious and Spiritual Life | Babson College
cards.access_notes: Open to all members of the Babson community for reflection and scheduled services.
